title: Is Tripo worth the money?
author: zayelion
selftext:
Title basically. Already spending $200 a month pushing Sol/Astra, and my graphics card is only 8GB VRAM. I kinda wanna add 3D models to my game but what Trellis is producing looks like trash.

Maybe I dont have the process down. Anyone have a solid tutorial for turning concept to decent models?

comments.author: Prior_Opportunity935
comments.body: Meshi works well for me, heard tripo was better tbh, id say its probably worth it.

replies.author: Next-Lunch-1994
replies.body: It is better but not much

replies.author: HeyYou_GetOffMyCloud
replies.body: The multiview smart mesh feature with tripo is insanely better than meshy. And segmentation for robots hard surface objects and characters is game ready

replies.author: Prior_Opportunity935
replies.body: Tripo provides better topology than meshi? Im impressed with what meshi does, but unless I rig/animate with meshi, the topology always leave room for improvement.

replies.author: HeyYou_GetOffMyCloud
replies.body:
My use case is game asset generation in quads, not 3D printing or hi detail capture. But certainly for game asset generation it's leagues better due to the simple fact it allows for multi image to be used in one asset. 

I can upload front back left right view and it will always be more accurate than something that's generating off one front view image.

replies.author: Prior_Opportunity935
replies.body: Ill have to give it a shot, my work flow rn, could use some improvement.

replies.author: Soul_Mate_4ever
replies.body: Yeah it’s worth it. I use meshy for rigging but tripo is much better at making models.

replies.author: Prior_Opportunity935
replies.body: Does tripo provides better topology? Im pretty new to using meshi, and if i dont rig the model in meshi, I get egregious topology.

comments.author: dilberry
comments.body: Yeah it is - make sure you remove the default coupon and apply one of the 60% off ones.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: Start with a $10 subscription for these services and see if it works

comments.author: lordpoee
comments.body: I don't mess with those. They feel scammy. Thy charge a monthly fee but you will burn through your credits in a hour and your left waiting 29 days to continue your work.

replies.author: MaqeSweden
replies.body: Sounds like you should be a bit more careful how you try new services and token spend.

replies.author: lordpoee
replies.body: It's not a care problem, I am quite good at token optimization. I simply think if you pay for a month of service you get a month of service. Feels deceptive to me. I'd advise not using any service that charges by the month that doesn't offer a month of service. Money poorly spent.

replies.author: MaqeSweden
replies.body: Most things paid monthly are not unlimited.

replies.author: twendah
replies.body: You can always reverse engineer it and make your own harness

replies.author: lordpoee
replies.body: Not a bad idea.

comments.author: DetectiveExisting803
comments.body: I already use Meshy, but people are using Tripo, so I’m going to test it. You can test both to get more results.

comments.author: CTXBITXH
comments.body: using tripo for a week now and its great honestly. Been only using the free tier tho because i dont have that much to generate and i use codex to generate the art, rig and animate, so i use it just for the mesh and for that its completely fine

comments.author: shitty_advice_BDD
comments.body:
I tested all the major ones and ended up back at Tripo.

https://i.redd.it/0fribqnohhzh1.png

replies.author: xoStardustt
replies.body: what tier do you run and how’s the usage?

replies.author: shitty_advice_BDD
replies.body:
I went with the lowest and as I ran out of tokens I upgraded to the next plan. I had a backlog of assets and models I needed to do though so once all those are done I might be able to go back to a lower plan. So, right now I I'm on their max plan but you get absolutely everything and a lot of freebies thrown in with it.

They also put contests together so you can win some tokens that way and stuff.

https://i.redd.it/9tuholahjhzh1.png

replies.author: konosmgr
replies.body: what's the workflow looking like, you also have to personally work on it on blender afterwards?

replies.author: shitty_advice_BDD
replies.body:
So I have chatgpt or grok draw it out and have it give me all four sides or just the front facing side. Then transfer to Tripo and if I have all four sides just put it in for the topology. Then if that looks good I have it textured and if that turns out good I have it texture that. Then I have Tripo rig the skeleton. 

Handoff to Codex and it updates the bones and everything through blender then adds it to the game. Sometimes there is a little back and forth but the learning curve overall is pretty shallow.

https://i.redd.it/1dw4sv9w7vzh1.png

comments.author: jungle_jimjim
comments.body: The smart mesh option is amazing imo, it captures every little detail and the models are max 25k quads, but the texturing is less good, so I either do that manually or let chatgpt do it

replies.author: UnarmedBobcat
replies.body: i would love to hear more about how you let gpt do it.. just unwrap give it the islands and references and ask for a flattened uv islands texture or what?

replies.author: jungle_jimjim
replies.body: Even simpler than that, I ask to texture it and to stay within the UVs. I also give it a reference picture and ask it to make a material for every color

comments.author: thenopeburger
comments.body: I have only tried having claude set up comfyui workflows that use turnaround sheets (made with ChatGPT) and turn them into rigged models. My workflow uses Tripo for part of it but not with a subscription. I just add credits to my comfy account and it pulls from there.

comments.author: sunnystormy64
comments.body: Hi3D v1.0 is out and fits within 8GB VRAM.

comments.author: GunpowderGuy
comments.body: relatedly what is the SOTA for 3d model generation. everyone recommends me closed solutions

comments.author: DigitalLeprechaun
comments.body: I haven't found a better option yet.

replies.author: zayelion
replies.body: What is your model?

comments.author: benharley
comments.body: Tripo is significantly better for more optimal low poly game meshes that need good edge flow. Not perfect by any means, but compared to meshy it’s night and day.

comments.author: azicre
comments.body: That depends on the prototype of the game you have made. Is it fun? Do your playtesters think it is fun? Are you going to turn it into a full product? If so it is worth spending money on that. If not, just use whatever is freely available.

comments.author: tuptain
comments.body: Loving Tripo, I use their API so my Claude can talk to them instead of me uploading images into a website.

replies.author: Bonelessgummybear
replies.body: Claude can use the website too

replies.author: AstonMartini13
replies.body: Does the API hit use your subscription credits or is it separate charges?

replies.author: tuptain
replies.body: Separate.

replies.author: konosmgr
replies.body: that's a problem since APIs for most thing AI related are priced like 10x more expensive than the same usage through subscription, is that true for trippo?

replies.author: tuptain
replies.body: $20 is 2000 tokens, each generation is about 40. You do get 50% more by going through Studio but it's not 10x.
